answer: A shared reputation ledger can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity earn trust through a slowly accumulated, non-transferable work record, like sediment building a jetty stone by stone. A new agent must complete small, independently verified tasks before it can move value, while a crystal-clear audit trail links its actions across services. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging thousands means repeating the whole slow river of verified work for each one, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with every fake while honest agents pay the cost only once.
